result.summary: This PR lets a descriptor wallet accept importdescriptors calls for public-only descriptors when the wallet already holds the corresponding private keys, substituting in the xprv/privkey instead of rejecting the import. It adds SubstituteMasterExtPubs to the descriptor classes to swap origin+xpub for a matching xprv, extends CWallet with GetKnownKeys to gather all known xprvs/keys, and wires this into ImportDescriptor. It also refactors importdescriptors' RPC-to-wallet plumbing (ImportDescriptorRequest/Result, error codes) as groundwork for non-RPC callers like a future GUI.
result.problem: Users who want to add a watch-style public descriptor to a wallet that already has the matching private keys currently must supply the private keys again in the descriptor, unnecessarily exposing key material. This mainly affects wallet users doing multisig setups, descriptor migrations, or coordinator/participant workflows where only public information should need to be shared.

open_concerns: Sjors proposed an alternative implementation (giving Parse access to the wallet's extended keys, simplified to HD keys only) as a possibly cleaner approach, but has not pushed for it to replace this PR's approach.
resolved_concerns: Dependency on #34861 (importdescriptors interface refactor) is resolved now that #34861 has merged.

result.card: This PR lets a descriptor wallet that holds private keys accept importdescriptors calls with the corresponding public-only descriptor, substituting in the wallet's own xprv or privkey instead of requiring the caller to expose key material. It solves a genuine privacy and usability gap tracked in long-open issue #27336, affecting users doing multisig setup or descriptor migration who currently must hand over private keys just to re-import a public descriptor. Three members (rkrux, polespinasa, Sjors) gave concept ACKs with stated reasons and nobody objected; Sjors floated an alternative implementation without blocking this one. It is still draft and has been force-pushed 11 times over several months, most recently 2026-09-14, but its stated dependency PR #34861 has since merged, removing the prior reason to wait. No material open reviewer request is blocking review of the current code.
